status: proposed 2026-10-05; changes published scores, so it waits for Max's ruling (cos decision). decided_on is the draft date; a release sets it to the ruling's date. proposed_regenerations.json and proposed_exclusions.json are alternatives: a release adopts one of them, not both.
basis: A reference that turns on an input or definition the prompt never states is excluded (reference_audit/2026-09-22 rule 4; reference_audit/2026-09-28 rule 4). The input here is an employer-arrangement fact with no engine input, as in r24 (who paid for the coverage behind listed disability benefits) and r25 (whether the federal output includes the net investment income tax), both recorded as reference_depends_on_unlisted_input.

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes, and says to exclude employer payroll taxes. Minnesota Paid Leave premiums "accrue and become payable by each employer" (Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subd. 1); the employer must pay at least 50 percent (small employers: at least a quarter of the full rate, subd. 5a), and employees pay through wage deductions only "the remaining portion, if any, of the premium not paid by the employer" (subd. 3), so the employee share runs from 0 to 0.44% of wages at the employer's choice. The reference reads 'mandatory' as the employee share the statute sets, withheld unless the employer elects to pay it, and counts the largest share the employer may deduct (mn_employee_paid_leave_contribution $127.60), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as the amount the law requires of the employee whatever the employer does, which is $0, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone: the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
exclusions.unlisted_input: whether the employer deducts the employee share of a state paid-leave or disability premium that the law lets it deduct but does not require, which decides whether that share is a mandatory employee state payroll tax
exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by classifying every state program in the payroll references from primary law (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll/program_classification.json) and sweeping all 1,984 outputs with the programs classified as optional employer pass-through left out of employee state payroll tax; that moves this output alone in its household and no other output. The law: Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subds. 1, 3 and 5a. The frozen value has been the reference since the first run (references generated 2026-06-12).

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes, and says to exclude employer payroll taxes. New York's covered employer must provide disability and Paid Family Leave coverage; it pays the disability cost beyond what it collects (N.Y. Workers' Compensation Law s. 210(1)), no employer is required to fund Paid Family Leave (s. 209(3)(b)), and the employer "is authorized to collect" employee contributions up to the statutory caps by payroll deduction (s. 209(4)). The Workers' Compensation Board says an employer "is allowed, but not required" to collect them. The reference reads 'mandatory' as the employee share the statute sets, withheld unless the employer elects to pay it, and counts the largest share the employer may deduct (ny_employee_disability_benefits_contribution $31.20, ny_employee_paid_family_leave_contribution $411.91), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as the amount the law requires of the employee whatever the employer does, which is $0, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone: the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
